hypothesis: A market-owned legacy RandomState, ID allocators, queue, agents and explicit lifecycle can preserve baseline event priority and both traces while independent live contexts interleave.
commit_role: Implementation and transport-fix commit; completed runtime report is saved in a following report-only commit.
change_summary: SimulationContext owns SimulationState, legacy master RNG, order/message counters, Kernel/agents/queue, collector and lifecycle; ContextVar selects ownership without global state swaps.
Separate build-time upstream patch routes implicit RNG constructors, wake-time utility, latency seeds and oracle megashocks/dense shocks through the owned legacy stream.
Bounded Kernel.runner(max_events) permits live-context interleaving including requeues and retains previous-time stop semantics.
Preserve baseline unused random_state_kernel draw and actual Kernel RandomState(0), including oracle master exponential draw in configuration order.
Capture Agent.logEvent on market-specific instances, preserve third-party overrides and exception restoration; use the Context API for simulate and serial batch.
Candidate batch contract repair drops disallowed root profile.json and keeps sub profiles; original baseline failure remains visible and requires separately recorded contract-only control.
Supply input-only runtime isolation diagnostic and sequential AB/BA runner with full developer gates, unchanged sanitation and exact both-trace comparisons.

Kernel.write_summary_log ignores skip_log; every Context now receives a unique absolute owned log directory without changing cwd. Default scratch is removed after termination/lifecycle failure; retained diagnostics keep per-context summary and agent files under log_root.

Add a separate resumable regression65 host wrapper with at most three spawned correctness workers, each capped at 3g. Serially revalidate all cached outputs before launches using original run_scenario; parent alone atomically persists each result and progress. Immutable image/input/ref/checker binding and owned-container recovery retained; standard regression/scorer/refs unchanged. Timing and profiling remain strictly sequential.

implementation_cost.notes: Moderate adapter/core integration, no rewritten matching engine or scoring code. Fast unbounded run avoids per-pop activation; interleaved stepping is diagnostic. Overlay successfully built from immutable baseline with unchanged Python packages, using copied source staging for GNU patch 2.8. Serial orchestration and shared-scratch transport recovery validated in actual runtime.

risks: Validated only pinned standard public scenarios and specified mixed-agent pair. Arbitrary third-party agents/config drivers/background callbacks remain outside the guarantee.
Upstream rmsc03/rmsc04 config drivers and legacy standalone build_config still use global np.random; SimulationContext uses neither path.
Arbitrary third-party direct np.random calls, class counters, module caches and background callbacks require explicit RNG/owner integration. No general thread-safety claim.
ComponentProfiler.instrument and legacy TraceCollector.capture retain class monkeypatches; live Context API uses instance capture and no profiler for interleaving.

Logger registry/handlers remain global. Kernel summary logging ignores skip_log, so the Context now always owns an absolute unique log directory. Third-party filesystem writes outside Kernel logging require separate integration; cwd is never changed.
Constructors outside state.activate use legacy global counters. Sharing one live context across concurrent threads/tasks is unsupported.

Batch sidecar repair is separate from context isolation: original baseline root profile failure was recorded, and the explicit contract-only control passed all gates with exact original traces in gates/warmup/three repeats/profile.
Local Mac ARM64 linux/amd64 measurements cannot be extrapolated to official Linux timing; no JIT is introduced.
